english.title: Racially / religiously aggravated harassment / alarm / distress by words / writing / behaviour
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[used threatening or abusive words or behaviour or disorderly behaviour]_
(B)_[displayed some writing, sign or other visible representation which was threatening or abusive]_

within the hearing or sight of a person likely to be caused harassment, alarm or distress, thereby, and the offence was

(C)_[racially]_
(D)_[religiously]_

aggravated within the terms of section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
english.legislation: Contrary to section 31(1)(c) and (5) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
used threatening/abusive words/behaviour/disorderly behaviour OR
displayed some writing/sign/other visible representation which was threatening/abusive
within the hearing/sight of a person likely to be caused harassment/alarm/distress thereby
and the offence was racially/religiously aggravated within the terms of s 28 Crime and Disorder Act 1998

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is NOT available in the magistrates court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence.
(ii) For the purpose of this offence section 28(1) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 shall have effect as if the person likely to be caused harassment, alarm or distress were the victim of the offence.
